steps.label: Hypanthodium
lines: Fig trees bear a hypanthodium - a closed,
steps.why: The name plus its one identifying feature - flowers hidden INSIDE a fleshy receptacle - is what makes the first mark complete.
common_mistakes: Writing hypanthium. The fig inflorescence is the hypanthodium.
steps.memory_tip: The fig you eat is the closed receptacle - the flowers are inside it.
steps.margin_note: Name + one line on the closed receptacle.

steps.label: Why Blastophaga visits
lines: hypanthodium to lay its eggs in the gall
While moving inside, it pollinates the fig
steps.why: The asked reason is egg-laying in the GALL flowers - the fig's special sterile flowers; pollination is the consequence the plant gains.
common_mistakes: Writing that the wasp comes only for nectar. It comes to lay eggs in the gall flowers.
steps.memory_tip: Gall flowers are the wasp's nursery; pollination is the fig's payment.
steps.margin_note: Say gall flowers by name; the pollination line completes the biology.
